text:
Priya: Heads-up: eu-central rack cluster had a latency tail this morning around 08:12. Multiple racks hit NIC egress > 88% and we saw NVLINK jitter + HBM evictions. Traced to tenant 'helix' running large nightly evals that kicked off concurrent prefill jobs.
Matt: rough. any quick isolations? can we qps-throttle their prefill or divert traffic?
Priya: We temporarily throttled their prefill qps which reduced p95 by ~30% but left a lot of waiting jobs. That degraded UX for important eval runs.
Hana: Long-term idea: "carousel containment" + thermocycle-limiter. Carousel = staggered ephemeral slices across racks so prefill warmers run asynchronously, not all at once. Thermocycle-limiter = controller that blocks new prefill allocations onto racks where thermal margin < threshold or recent NVLINK jitter exceeded.
Egor: So carousel staggers warmers across N racks with offsets, like a moving window. Warmers start at t0, t0+delay, t0+2*delay... avoids synchronized spikes. How long is delay?
Hana: Prototype: 90s delay between slices, 6m total cycle (4 racks * 90s). Warmers limited to 1 concurrent prefill per tenant per rack. Prefill QPS cap enforced globally.
Matt: Scheduler changes? need tagging and scoring. Also need to ensure we don't evict enterprise dedicated hosts.
Egor: Scheduler responsibilities: 1) filter candidate racks by thermocycle score (egress_headroom, thermal_margin, nvlink_jitter), 2) apply offset schedule from carousel controller, 3) annotate allocation with expected warmup window so proxy can queue prefill jobs accordingly.
Priya: Ops question: what metrics and alerts trigger the controller? my list: per-rack egress_utilization > 75% sustained 30s, nvlink_jitter_rate > baseline*1.5, hbm_evictions increase > 3 in 5m, kvcache_miss_rate spike.
Hana: Agreed. Also add a soft-block for racks with recent thermal trips. We'll use a sliding window so short transients don't block forever.
Tess: cost/time tradeoffs? Carousel increases token churn from kvcache cold misses but avoids a full dedicated carveout. We need delta numbers for finance.
Hana: Benchmarks: on testbed, carousel reduced peak per-rack egress by ~35% and p95 latency stabilized; overall prefill tokens rose ~12% due to extra cache misses. Net expected billing delta ~+9% tokens during carousel events vs current outage baseline.
Matt: Still cheaper than standing up extra dedicated slices for each noisy tenant. But we should expose opt-out for paid enterprise tenants.
Priya: Can we implement a grace mode where we try small QPS taper before carousel? sometimes a little backoff resolves it.
Egor: Yes: flow: detect surge -> attempt local taper (backoff 30-60s) -> if persisted, enable carousel for tenant -> monitor -> if repeated 4x/day then notify sales for dedicated offer.
Dev Deploy Bot: deploy: feature/carousel-controller queued -> will run canary for tenant 'carousel-canary' in eu-central at 02:00 UTC.
ops-bot: runtime flags created: carousel.enabled, carousel.delay_seconds, carousel.max_concurrent_prefills_per_rack, thermocycle.thermal_margin_threshold.
Tess: Need a prometheus snippet for alerts and scoring, e.g.:
```
(sum by(rack)(rate(egress_bytes[1m]))) / rack_capacity_egress > 0.75
or increase(hbm_evictions[5m]) > 3
```
Priya: Also add nvlink_jitter metric:
```
avg_over_time(nvlink_jitter[2m]) > 0.02
```
Hana: Canary plan: enable carousel for 'carousel-canary' tenant during low window, track p95, egress_headroom, and tokens. If p95 improves and tokens within budget, roll to auto-enroll noisy tenants behind a preference flag.
Matt: Implementation owners? Hana takes controller + orchestration, Egor handles scheduler scoring & integration, Tess will own cost model + billing hooks, Priya owns canary observation and incident comms.
Priya: I'll create a short runbook: detect -> try taper -> enable carousel -> if no improvement after 2 cycles escalate to dedicated carveout + billing action.
Tess: I'll draft billing rule: if carousel runs > 3x/day for a tenant, auto-generate cost estimate and SRE ticket offering dedicated pool with expected monthly cost and latency gain.
Egor: One more thought: prefer racks with cooler inlet temps and lower recent GPU utilization. Score = alpha*egress_headroom + beta*thermal_margin + gamma*(1 - recent_gpu_util). We'll tune alpha/beta/gamma in canary.
Hana: Good. Also add a metric to measure carousel effectiveness: "carousel_peak_reduction_pct" and "carousel_token_overhead_pct" so we can quantify impact over time.
Matt: timeline: 1) alerting + metric plumbing (48h), 2) controller + scoring (5d), 3) scheduler integration + feature flags (3d), 4) canary (24-48h), 5) review + opt-in policy (1w).
Priya: ok let's spin up PRs. tagging owners @Hana @Egor @Tess. I'll post canary updates here.
Priya: thanks team. will post incident follow-up after first canary run. :party_parrot:
